text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
- The Swiss were bankers and financial dealers for the Nazis, according to the Eizenstat Report that was released on Wednesday in Washington.
- Telecommunications group Ascom will sell its U.S. subsidiary Nexion to Japan's Fujitsu Network Communications Ltd for some $130 million.
- U.S. Transportation Department approved the code sharing extension between Delta Air Lines, Swissair, Sabena and Austrian Airlines, which will begin on June 1.
- Helbling Group's five management consulting and engineering firms reported a 6.9 percent sales increase to 51.4 million Swiss francs for 1996.
- Zuercher Cantonal Bank reduced its inflation forecast for 1997 from one percent to zero percent, mainly because of lower import taxes.

- One day after the public release of the Eizenstat Report, U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato demanded the revision of the 1946 Washington Agreement with Switzerland that settled Allied claims against Berne over Swiss gold deals with Nazi Germany.
- Switzerland's image is worsening in the American press with Wednesday's release of the Eizenstat Report.
